t: 3683. Earliest Time to Finish One Task — Editorial
o:
## Understanding the problem
Each task starts at sᵢ and takes tᵢ time; tasks run concurrently. Find the earliest finish time, i.e. min(sᵢ + tᵢ). Example 1: min(1+6, 2+3) = 5; example 2: all finish at 200.

Trivial scan suffices given n ≤ 100.
k: Tasks run in parallel, so no scheduling interaction — just minimize s + t.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear scan of s + t
a.i: Accumulate the minimum of start-plus-duration over all tasks in one pass.
s: For each task, best = min(best, s + t).

w: Nothing to optimize; the only mistake possible is misreading the problem as sequential execution. Follow-up: earliest time all tasks finish (max, not min), or tasks with dependencies.
